00420.title: Doxorubicin and cisplatin for osteosarcoma: treatment and checks
00420.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00420.setting: Chemotherapy before and after surgery for osteosarcoma
00420.summary: Doxorubicin 25 mg/m² is given on days 1, 2 and 3; cisplatin 100 mg/m² on day 1. The reference course contains six 21-day cycles, usually three before surgery and three afterwards, with pathology review. Treatment dates and doses depend on recovery and the specialist plan.

00463.title: Methotrexate, doxorubicin and cisplatin for osteosarcoma: treatment and checks
00463.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00463.setting: High-grade osteosarcoma of an extremity or axial skeleton, excluding craniofacial sites, with all disease sites amenable to complete surgical resection; national eligibility age 40 years or younger
00463.summary: The reference plan is not a repeating 21-day cycle. Before surgery, doxorubicin 37.5 mg/m² and cisplatin 60 mg/m² are each given on days 1 and 2 of weeks 1 and 6; methotrexate 12 g/m² is given on day 1 of weeks 4, 5, 9 and 10. Surgery is planned for reference week 11. Afterwards, doxorubicin is given on days 1 and 2 of weeks 12, 17, 22 and 26; cisplatin on days 1 and 2 of weeks 12 and 17; methotrexate on day 1 of weeks 15, 16, 20, 21, 24, 25, 28 and 29. Actual dates depend on surgery, recovery, drug clearance and safety review.

Reduced urine, severe mouth ulcers or diarrhoea, new neurological symptoms or delayed methotrexate clearance needs urgent specialist assessment.

00100.title: Mifamurtide after osteosarcoma surgery: treatment and checks
00100.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00100.setting: High-grade, resectable, nonmetastatic osteosarcoma after macroscopically complete resection, alongside postoperative multi-agent chemotherapy; national age eligibility 2–30 years
00100.summary: Mifamurtide 2 mg/m² is infused over 1 hour after complete resection and surgical recovery. Give two infusions each week for the first 12 weeks, at least 3 days apart, then one infusion weekly for another 24 weeks: 48 infusions over 36 weeks. This timetable runs separately from the chemotherapy calendar. The specialist team confirms the actual postoperative start and any delays.

milestones.why: Mifamurtide stimulates innate immune cells to help act against remaining osteosarcoma cells after complete surgery. It is an additional postoperative treatment discussed with the patient and family, alongside chemotherapy.

Do not wait eight hours to seek advice for fever or sudden illness. Severe wheeze, breathing difficulty, chest pain or faintness needs urgent assessment.

00596.title: Ifosfamide and etoposide for Ewing sarcoma or osteosarcoma: treatment and checks
00596.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00596.setting: Relapsed Ewing sarcoma, or treatment of osteosarcoma under the national source indication
00596.summary: Etoposide 100 mg/m² is infused over 60 minutes, followed by ifosfamide 1,800 mg/m² over 60 minutes, on each of days 1–5. Courses repeat every 21 days for up to seven cycles while benefit and tolerability justify treatment. Mesna is given before each ifosfamide infusion and at 4 and 8 hours measured from its START.

00680.title: High-dose ifosfamide for recurrent Ewing sarcoma or relapsed osteosarcoma: treatment and checks
00680.status: Source-reconciled feasibility draft; independent clinician, pharmacy and patient review pending.
00680.setting: Recurrent or primary refractory Ewing sarcoma, or relapsed osteosarcoma
00680.summary: Ifosfamide 3,000 mg/m² is infused over 24 hours on each of days 1–5, giving five consecutive 24-hour infusions. Repeat every 21 days for a maximum of four cycles unless progression or unacceptable toxicity stops treatment sooner. Mesna starts before the first infusion, continues throughout the five-day treatment and includes a final dose on day 6 after the last ifosfamide infusion.

milestones.when: Five consecutive 24-hour ifosfamide infusions; every 21 days, maximum 4 cycles
